thread:
alex_cs: Quick heads-up — Nebula dedicated bring-up is next Tue. We need guardrails for quota + autoscale smoke tests. Can we lock down a preflight checklist? :spiral_calendar:

jordan_sre: 👍 what's the expected steady RPS and burst pattern? also which region/pool will they be on?
maria_pm: Nebula expects ~800 RPS steady for search endpoints, bursts to ~2k for short windows (30s-2m). They'll be in eu-west-1 reserved pool A. SLA target: 99.95% p99 < 300ms.
sam_ml: Model is gpt-big-8k, KV cache matters. We'll want to prime prefix cache and test cold vs hot-starts. Also recommend quantized variant for cost — but validate quality.
jordan_sre: Ok. Drafting checklist: 1) quota limits (concurrency + token/sec) 2) warmup priming script 3) autoscale policy test 4) failover fallback validation 5) telemetry assertions (errors, p95/p99, queue length).
alex_cs: Can you paste the autoscale test commands so CS can run if SRE is tied up?
jordan_sre: Sure — quick k6 smoke snippet below. Run from a bastion in eu-west-1 against the reserved endpoint.
```bash
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 2m script.js 
# ramp to burst: ramping to 2k vus over 30s, hold 90s, then ramp down
```
sam_ml: For priming, run a sequence of typical prefixes + a few long-context samples. Example curl loop: `for p in prefixes.txt; do curl -s -X POST $ENDPOINT -d "$p"; done` — that should populate KV cache.
eng-sre-bot: [scheduled-test] capacity-smoke: created test job 3098765432/nebula-preflight in eu-west-1, window Tue 09:00-11:00 UTC.
alex_cs: Tagged Nebula PM and ops. @maria_pm can you confirm the preferred window? Ops wants non-business hours but they prefer morning.
maria_pm: Morning EU is fine. Let's pick Tue 09:30 UTC. We'll do a short sanity at 09:30 then full smoke at 10:00.
jordan_sre: Timeline + owners: 09:30 quick warmup (sam_ml + alex_cs), 10:00 autoscale ramp (jordan_sre + eng-sre), 10:30 soak + fallback test (eng-sre).
alex_cs: Noted. Quota guardrails: set concurrency cap 400, token/sec cap 300k initially. If autoscale behaves, we can relax after sign-off.
sam_ml: Add a quality check: run 100 eval prompts and compute KL/ROUGE diffs vs baseline. If > threshold, abort.
jordan_sre: We'll wire up health checks: error rate alert >0.5% and p99 > 400ms triggers immediate throttle and rollback to hosted variant.
alex_cs: Recording action items: - jordan_sre to push k6 script + runbook (due EOD Fri) - sam_ml to share priming script and eval set - maria_pm to confirm stakeholders & sign-off - eng-sre-bot to create test jobs & alert hooks.
maria_pm: I'll loop in Nebula's infra lead and legal for any compliance checklist.
eng-sre-bot: [reminder] test window Tue 09:30 UTC (2d left)
jordan_sre: One more: plan for simulated region failover — during the soak we'll trigger a routing fallback to fallback-model (lower-cost variant) to verify graceful degradation. Have rollback playbook ready.
alex_cs: Great. Who's running the post-test summary? I'll compile and send to Nebula with next steps.
sam_ml: I'll run the eval and post quality numbers.
jordan_sre: I'll post perf dashboard link + logs after the run.
alex_cs: Final check — anyone foresee quota negotiation issues with procurement? If so flag now.
maria_pm: Procurement already agreed base commit. They may ask to increase concurrency after go-live; that's fine, we'll document the process.
eng-sre-bot: [completed] capacity-smoke job 3098765432/nebula-preflight executed. Results uploaded to /artifacts/3098765432.
jordan_sre: Quick recap: smoke passed. Peak RPS 2100, p95 85ms, p99 170ms, errors 0.14%. Autoscale policy scaled from 1->6 nodes within 45s. Fallback verified (invoked successfully).
sam_ml: Eval: quality delta vs baseline within acceptable band. No regression alerts.
alex_cs: Awesome — sending handoff doc + renewal health note. Thanks everyone :tada:"
